title: The Workshop That Sold Its Time
fact_notes: 人物・具体的な出来事は架空の思考実験・教材例。実在の調査・統計を示すものではない。制作台帳は来歴確認用。

sentences.en: A fictional repair workshop offered to restore damaged wooden furniture for customers in its neighborhood.
sentences.ja: 架空の修理工房は近所の顧客向けに傷んだ木製家具を修復すると申し出た。

sentences.en: The owner published a price list based on the type of object brought to the shop.
sentences.ja: 経営者は持ち込まれる品の種類に基づく価格表を公開した。

sentences.en: For instance, repairing a chair always cost the same amount regardless of its condition.
sentences.ja: 例えば椅子の修理は状態にかかわらずいつも同額だった。

sentences.en: The simple arrangement made it easy for potential customers to understand the price before visiting.
sentences.ja: 簡単な仕組みで見込み客は来店前に価格を理解しやすかった。

sentences.en: However, the owner gradually discovered that the actual time required for each repair varied considerably.
sentences.ja: しかし修理ごとに実際に必要な時間がかなり異なると徐々に分かった。

sentences.en: Some chairs needed only a minor adjustment, whereas others required extensive work on several damaged parts.
sentences.ja: 軽い調整だけで済む椅子もあれば、傷んだ複数の部分の大がかりな作業が必要な椅子もあった。

sentences.en: The workshop was often busy, yet its income was sometimes insufficient to cover the expenses of operating the business.
sentences.ja: 工房は忙しいことが多かったが収入が事業の運営費を賄えないときもあった。

sentences.en: The owner realized that accepting more orders would not necessarily improve the financial situation.
sentences.ja: 注文を増やしても必ずしも財務状況は改善しないと気づいた。

sentences.en: Before changing the prices, the owner recorded the amount of labor and materials used for different categories of repair.
sentences.ja: 価格変更前に修理の種類ごとの労働と材料の量を記録した。

sentences.en: She also considered the importance of giving customers reliable estimates before beginning their work.
sentences.ja: 作業開始前に顧客へ信頼できる見積もりを示す重要性も考えた。

sentences.en: Instead of introducing a complicated hourly charge with no upper limit, she created several service levels according to the expected difficulty.
sentences.ja: 上限のない複雑な時間料金を導入せず、予想難度に応じたサービス段階を作った。

sentences.en: Each estimate explained what was included and what additional work would require the customer's approval.
sentences.ja: 各見積もりは含まれるものと顧客の承認が必要な追加作業を説明した。

sentences.en: The revised arrangement allowed customers to decide whether an expensive repair was worthwhile before making a commitment.
sentences.ja: 修正した仕組みで顧客は契約前に高額な修理が価値あるものか判断できた。

sentences.en: It also helped the owner reserve enough time for jobs that could not be completed quickly.
sentences.ja: すぐ終えられない作業の時間を十分確保する助けにもなった。

sentences.en: Nevertheless, she recognized that unexpected damage could still create uncertainty even after a careful initial examination.
sentences.ja: それでも慎重な初期検査後に予想外の損傷が不確実性を生むことも認識した。

sentences.en: She therefore established a procedure for discussing changes with customers rather than silently increasing the final charge.
sentences.ja: そこで最終料金を黙って増やさず顧客と変更を話し合う手順を作った。

sentences.en: The workshop's experience illustrates why the quantity of completed transactions is not always a sufficient measure of business performance.
sentences.ja: 工房の経験は成立した取引の量だけでは事業の成績を十分測れない場合がある理由を示す。

sentences.en: A business must consider the resources consumed by each transaction as well as the revenue it generates.
sentences.ja: 事業では各取引が生む収入だけでなく消費する資源も考える必要がある。

sentences.en: Clear pricing can help both businesses and customers understand the expectations attached to an exchange.
sentences.ja: 明確な価格設定は事業者と顧客が取引に伴う期待を理解する助けになる。

sentences.en: The owner's improvement involved not simply charging more, but creating a better connection between the price and the work actually performed.
sentences.ja: 改善は単に値上げすることでなく、価格と実際に行った作業をよりよく結びつけることだった。

questions.explanation_ja: 家具の種類で価格を定めた。

questions.prompt: What was an advantage of the original system?
options: Customers could understand the cost easily.
questions.explanation_ja: 価格が分かりやすかった。

questions.prompt: Why might extra orders fail to help?
options: Customers always agreed to pay more.
Some orders might consume more resources than their price justified.
questions.explanation_ja: 価格に対して作業負担が大きい場合がある。

options: Charged the same price for every object.
Created service levels based on expected difficulty.
questions.explanation_ja: 難度に応じた段階を導入。

questions.prompt: What happened when additional work arose?
options: The final fee was secretly doubled.
All repair work was canceled automatically.
Changes would be discussed with customers.
Customers were forbidden to ask questions.
questions.explanation_ja: 変更を顧客と話し合う。

options: Unexpected damage could be found after an examination.
All furniture had already been replaced.
Service levels could predict every possible problem.
questions.explanation_ja: 検査後も予想外の損傷があり得る。

options: More orders always guarantee higher profit.
Prices and business performance should reflect resources used as well as sales.
Customers should never be informed of changes.
questions.explanation_ja: 売上と資源消費の両方を考慮する。

paraphrases.source: For instance, repairing a chair always cost the same amount regardless of its condition.
paraphrases.rewrite: Every chair had the same repair price no matter how damaged it was.

paraphrases.source: Some chairs needed only a minor adjustment, whereas others required extensive work on several damaged parts.
paraphrases.rewrite: Some chairs were easy to fix, while others needed substantial repairs.

paraphrases.source: Instead of introducing a complicated hourly charge with no upper limit, she created several service levels according to the expected difficulty.
paraphrases.rewrite: She offered levels of service based on difficulty rather than an unlimited hourly rate.

paraphrases.source: A business must consider the resources consumed by each transaction as well as the revenue it generates.
paraphrases.rewrite: Businesses need to assess both the money earned from a deal and the resources used to complete it.
paraphrases.explanation_ja: 収入と消費資源を評価。
